headline: Cross-cohort and cross-platform evaluation frames claims in omics and tabular biomedical prediction
label: Validation Design Biomedical Prediction
summary: Five preprints pair new predictors with cross-platform, benchmark or external-cohort tests, while one reports a single 184-patient cohort.
synthesis: The common thread is how evaluation design bounds what a biomedical predictive claim supports. PRTS predicts clinical endpoints from bulk transcriptomes across diseases and platforms without per-cohort training. TabBioMed standardizes preprocessing over 94 public tabular datasets and compares 23 models; foundation models lead, but tree-based methods remain competitive. SNOWS tests transfer to CGGA, raising C-index from 0.691 to 0.712. SOSM reports a C-index of 0.768 on a single 184-patient ccRCC cohort, a narrower evidence base. Elflow is benchmarked on public flow and CyTOF datasets. The new element is a shift toward cross-platform, external-cohort and standardized comparison. These items do not establish whether curated public benchmarks reflect generalization under deployment conditions.
